preferredWrite.decision: The request shape is verified live (create + readback + delete, 2026-08-16). importSafe is true: the guest confirmation email is covered by the site-wide mute (verified muted during the probe). Note that the event must be published first (draft-events-reject-rsvps).

contactFields.notes: Guest email on the RSVP create body — required, format-validated, and the key Wix uses to create/match a CRM contact.

pitfalls.summary: RSVP creation emails the guest a confirmation unless disableNotifications is set (the domain's registration-notifications-default-on pitfall). Setting disableNotifications:true is harmless; it is not required. Covered by site mute: when getSiteMuteState reads muted:true, this is not a reason to block, skip, delay or warn about the entity.

Probed 2026-08-16: disableNotifications:true is accepted, persisted and echoed on create and GET; the docs describe it only as "Whether notifications are disabled". Covered by site mute: when getSiteMuteState reads muted:true, this is not a reason to block, skip, delay or warn about the entity.
RE-VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-27: an RSVP on a DRAFT event fails 400 EVENT_NOT_FOUND. A source draft that has RSVPs is therefore created published.

CORRECTED 2026-08-16 (live): the earlier claim that RSVPs do not touch CRM is wrong. Creating one RSVP produced a new contact for the guest email with sourceType WIX_EVENTS. An RSVP import therefore writes into Contacts as a side effect — it can duplicate contacts imported by crm/contact, and it means RSVP volume is contact volume. Reconcile guest emails against the contact crosswalk before importing RSVPs, and count the contact writes in the plan. (Method note: a Contacts V4 query filtered on info.emails.email returned zero rows for a contact that plainly exists — filter fields are a closed list per endpoint, so verify by listing, not by an unsupported filter.)

A freshly created event comes back with registration.status CLOSED_AUTOMATICALLY (no sale/RSVP window open), and create-rsvp defines RSVPS_CLOSED / RSVPS_NOT_STARTED / GUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED / RSVP_LIMIT_EXCEEDED failures. The 2026-08-16 probe passed options.ignoreResponseStatus:true and options.ignoreLimits:true and succeeded; which of the two was strictly required was not isolated. A historical-guest import should pass both deliberately and disclose it — they override the site's own registration rules.

rsvp.form.inputValues must use the input names from the event's form (GET /events/v3/events/{id}?fields=FORM), honour mandatory inputs for YES responses, and stay inside predefined options, else INVALID_FORM_RESPONSE. The probe sent firstName/lastName/email and they round-tripped. options.ignoreFormValidation exists as an escape hatch for lossy source data. Additional guests require the event form to carry a GUEST_CONTROL control.

VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-27: with ignoreResponseStatus + ignoreLimits, a repeated email on one event is ACCEPTED as a second RSVP (no MEMBER_EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED). Dedupe the source guest list by email per event before writing, and recover a lost response with findRsvpsByEmail (lists the event, `email` is not filterable on Query Rsvps) before any resend.

The event's registration.initialType must be RSVP and is immutable — a TICKETING event can never accept RSVPs (428 INVALID_EVENT_TYPE). Choose the registration type when creating the event from the source data.

VERIFIED LIVE 2026-10-27: an ended published event accepts RSVPs only with options.ignoreResponseStatus (without it, or with ignoreLimits alone: 428 RSVPS_CLOSED). createRsvp sets both overrides by default.

mappingGuidance: Dependencies: events/event must be published for the RSVP API; the registration form is the event's own (Create Event makes it), so it is not a separate dependency and an RSVP waits only for its own event; crm/contact must exist when matching the RSVP attendee by email.
Create the event first with registration.initialType RSVP, PUBLISH it, and use its crosswalked ID in eventId — draft events are invisible to this API.
disableNotifications:true may be set on every create call (harmless); the site mute is what covers guest email.

Map source attendee records (e.g. Event Tickets RSVPs) to firstName/lastName/email/status (YES | NO | WAITLIST) and additionalGuestDetails.guestCount/guestNames; build form.inputValues from the event's form controls.
Plan the CRM impact: each RSVP creates or matches a contact (sourceType WIX_EVENTS), so sequence RSVPs after crm/contact and reconcile by email.

evidence.note: object page: eventId, firstName/lastName/email, status, totalGuests
disableNotifications is a field on the rsvp object (not a query param); described only as "Whether notifications are disabled" — no statement about the guest confirmation email
The docs survey identified the RSVP import surface.

Verified live on a muted site: RSVP creation against a draft event returned EVENT_NOT_FOUND; after publication, creation with disableNotifications:true and ignoreResponseStatus/ignoreLimits succeeded. The flag persisted on readback and Wix created a contact with sourceType WIX_EVENTS. Notification delivery remains unverified because the site was muted and the test address was undeliverable. Probe records were deleted afterward.
Verified live 2026-10-27 on a throwaway site created for the probe (notifications muted): create, read back, query, past dates, category assignment.

notes: Authored 2026-08-11 from the docs-survey gap (RSVP V2). The write shape was promoted to verified-live on 2026-08-16. importSafe is true: guest email is covered by the site mute. The same probe found two contradictions in the original entry: draft events reject RSVPs, and RSVP creation does create a CRM contact.
